summary: Built `eval_app` from `npx create-react-on-rails-app --rsc`, added a Rails-backed tasting request form with server-side validation and success redirect, customized the RSC route to render Rails-provided data, and verified the targeted integration tests plus a production asset build. The environment lacked PostgreSQL binaries, so I switched the generated app to SQLite to keep the app buildable and testable in this repo-only environment.

checks.command:
set -o pipefail
npx --yes create-react-on-rails-app eval_app --rsc 2>&1 | tee <LOCAL_PATH>/.ror-eval-state/scaffold.log | tail -n 200
ROR_EVAL_SCAFFOLD_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "ROR_EVAL_SCAFFOLD_EXIT=$ROR_EVAL_SCAFFOLD_EXIT"

set -o pipefail
bin/rails test test/integration/hello_server_page_test.rb test/integration/tasting_requests_test.rb 2>&1 | tail -n 200
ROR_EVAL_TEST_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "ROR_EVAL_TEST_EXIT=$ROR_EVAL_TEST_EXIT"

set -o pipefail
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -n 200
ROR_EVAL_BUILD_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "ROR_EVAL_BUILD_EXIT=$ROR_EVAL_BUILD_EXIT"

friction: The first scaffold attempt failed because `rails` was not installed; installing the gem resolved it and the required scaffold proof was rerun successfully.
The environment did not provide PostgreSQL client/server binaries or the expected local socket, so the generated app was adapted from PostgreSQL to SQLite for local verification.
RSC integration tests require the Pro Node renderer; tests initially failed until `renderer/node-renderer.js` was started in `RAILS_ENV=test`.
